purpose: Compact newcomer map. It points to existing canonical owners instead of copying domain behavior.

structure.purpose: Repository operating contract; read first. Operational harness does not modify it.
Canonical repository-family and cross-domain harness registries, policies, schemas, fixtures, and workflows.
Operational harness spine: task routing, validator discovery, artifacts, reports, and handoff.
Harness-owned materialize/preflight/execute composition that prevents clipboard mutation between OpenCode sprint gates.
Device/platform profiles and focused profile harnesses.
Windows-first GNHF control-plane tooling and its contracts.
Pi operational harness and experimental orchestration contracts.
PowerShell contract validators and read-only status probes.
Dependency-light Python and Bash contracts used by Linux/Windows CI.
Durable public coordination records; plans are not implementation.

entrypoints.when: Fresh agent or operator needs the operational front door.
Need a read-only English/JSON snapshot and handoff artifacts.
An OpenCode bounded sprint needs preflight and execution without recopying or re-reading a mutable clipboard prompt.
Need the existing aggregate offline app harness on Windows.
Need the Windows startup/readiness launcher; runtime proof is separate.

build.reason: AgentSwitchboard has no single conventional compile/build step; domain installers and launchers own their own validation.

deploy.reason: No generic deploy is authorized by this harness. Profile/install/runtime lanes use their own explicit operator contracts.

knownTraps: Do not assume the current shell is inside a Git checkout; resolve repository identity before calling git rev-parse.
Do not call .Trim() on command output until the command exit code and non-null output are checked.
PowerShell interactive paste can execute a completed if block before a following standalone else block; keep } else { in the same parsed statement or execute a tracked .ps1 file as one unit.
Do not use a clipboard-backed OpenCode PlanOnly preflight and then launch later from the clipboard again; preflight and execution must be bound to one materialized prompt artifact and digest.
Do not infer runtime readiness from repository, package, process, SSH, tmux-name, or CI presence.
Do not run a domain validator merely because its filename exists; select the owning workflow and proof ceiling first.
Do not install Git hooks implicitly. The operational pre-commit and pre-push helpers are opt-in only.
Do not put generated operational reports inside the repository.
Do not clean, reset, stash, force-push, or rewrite history to make a validation result look clean.
Do not use the operational harness as authority to mutate AGENTS.md, secrets, product code, live targets, providers, or credentials.
